summary: Edeltraud Harzer works in indology and philosophy. She studied at Charles University, the University of Washington, and under traditional teachers Shree Narayan Mishra and Ram Shankar Bhattacharya. She held posts at Puget Sound, Washington, Stanford, Indiana, and UT Austin (1998).

Edith Wyschogrod was a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who studied at Hunter College (~1953–1957) and Columbia University (~1964–1970). She taught Lucy Annette Jones and served on the faculty at Rice University (~1992–2004).
Edmond Yee works in religious studies and sinology. He served as a faculty member at Pacific Lutheran Theological Seminary (~1984–2009) and the Graduate Theological Union (~1984–2009).

Edmund Hardy was an indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and religious studies specialist. He studied at Heidelberg University (~1872–1874) and Humboldt University (~1874–1876), later serving as professor at the University of Freiburg (1885–1893) and the University of Fribourg (~1893–1898).

Edmund Leach was a scholar of religious studies and other fields who studied at Clare College, LSE, and under Bronislaw Malinowski. He held a post at the University of Cambridge (~1953–1978) and taught Geoffrey Samuel, Caroline Humphrey, and Fredrik Barth.
Edmund Nathaniel Snyder was an indologist. He graduated as valedictorian from Harvard University in 1886 and studied under Albrecht Weber and Hermann Oldenberg.

Edo Shonin works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. In 2015, he was attested as a research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University and as Research Director at the Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research.

Eduard Hermann was a linguist and indologist who studied under Berthold Delbrück (~1891–1893). He taught Hans-Werner Köhler and held posts at the University of Kiel (~1913–1917), Goethe University Frankfurt (~1917–1924), and the University of Göttingen (~1924–1938).

Eduard Müller was a scholar of indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He completed his Inauguraldissertation at Leipzig University (~1871–1874) and served as a professor at the University of Bern (~1886–1908).

Eduard Sachau worked in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Kiel and Leipzig under Hermann Brockhaus. He held posts at the University of Vienna, Frederick William/Humboldt University, and directed the Seminar for Oriental Languages.

Eduard Sievers was a linguist who studied at Leipzig University and Frederick William University Berlin. He taught Carl Gaedicke and held professorships and posts at Jena (1871–1883), Tübingen (1883–1887), Halle-Wittenberg (1887–1892), and Leipzig (1892–1922).

Eduardo Francisco Freyre Roach works in Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Buddhist Studies at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2014), where he studied under supervisors Y. Karunadasa and Georgios T. Halkias.
Edward Albert Gait was a scholar of history, archaeology, and indology. He studied at University College London (~1880–1882) and founded the Bihar Research Society in 1914.

Edward Backhouse Eastwick worked in indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He was educated at Charterhouse School and Merton College, later serving as Professor of Hindústání at East India Company College (~1845–1857) and at the Foreign Office (~1860–1863).

Edward Byles Cowell studied at Oxford under Horace Hayman Wilson. An indologist and Buddhist studies scholar, he served as professor at Presidency University, principal at Sanskrit College, and professor at the University of Cambridge, teaching Cecil Bendall and M. N. Bhattacharyya.
Edward C. Dimock was a scholar of indology and religious studies. He studied at Yale University (~1950–1953) and held a post at the University of Chicago (~1957–1992).

Edward Clive Bayley was a scholar of indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at East India Company College and Haileybury and Imperial Service College (~1840–1842) and entered the Indian Civil Service in 1842.

Edward Conze was a Buddhist studies and indology scholar who studied at Bonn and Cologne. He taught Richard Hugh Robinson and held posts at the University of London, Buddhist Society, UC Berkeley, Lancaster, and the University of Washington.

Edward Denison Ross studied at UCL, where he later held the Chair of Persian (~1896–1901). Working in Iranian/Central Asian studies, tibetology, and history, he taught Zuicho Tachibana and held posts at the British Museum and SOAS (~1916–1937).

Edward Elbridge Salisbury studied at Yale and under Woolsey, Burnouf, de Sacy, de Tassy, Bopp, and Lassen. A scholar of indology and linguistics, he was professor at Yale (1841–1854), taught William Dwight Whitney, and served the American Oriental Society.
